# Flutter / Dart

- `DeeplinkHandler.handle` takes `required DeeplinkSource source` with no default and never throws; a handler that cannot route a link answers `false`, and the first handler whose `canHandle` is true ends the chain. A default would let a handler treat a crafted OS link like a server-authored push payload.
- Reach `magic_notifications` only through `app.bound('notifications')` and dynamic access in `OneSignalDeeplinkHandler`: never import it or add it to `pubspec.yaml`, since it is an optional companion. `boot()` runs in magic's bare provider loop, so the wiring catches, reports through `Log.error` and lets boot continue; an uncaught throw aborts every later provider.
- Wait for the router with `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized().endOfFrame`, captured once before the first link can arrive (`DeeplinkServiceProvider.boot`, `OneSignalDeeplinkHandler.setup`), never `Future.delayed(Duration.zero, ...)`: a zero-duration timer loses the link on any slower boot, and `endOfFrame` schedules a frame when the scheduler is idle.
